about.title: Redwood City Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You are on the ground in a grocery aisle, a parking garage, or an apartment stairwell somewhere in Redwood City, and your first thought is simply whether you can get up. The questions arrive later: who was responsible for that wet floor, that loose step, that unlit walkway? Under California law, premises liability turns on notice. The owner or manager must have known, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and then failed to fix it or warn you. Proving that requires evidence that tends to vanish fast, which is why photos, witness names, and a prompt request to preserve surveillance footage carry so much weight. Redwood City serves as the San Mateo County seat, home to roughly 85,000 residents and busy commercial stretches along El Camino Real, Woodside Road, and Middlefield Road. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Redwood City Residents Turn to LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Attorneys Who Build the Notice Case
items.desc: Winning a California premises claim usually means showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys we connect you with know how to gather inspection logs, maintenance records, and prior complaints to establish that.

items.title: Deadlines Tracked From Day One
items.desc: Most premises claims in California carry a two-year filing window, but if the property belongs to the City of Redwood City, San Mateo County, or another public entity, the deadline is far shorter. Getting connected early protects your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Handled Honestly
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so a claim is not lost just because you were partly distracted or wearing the wrong shoes. Your recovery may be reduced by your share of responsibility, and a good attorney works to keep that share fair.

items.question: I fell inside a county building in downtown Redwood City. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It does. Redwood City is the San Mateo County seat, and falls on property owned by the county, the city, or another government entity follow a separate process. You generally must file an administrative claim with that entity first, and the window to do so is typically six months rather than two years. An attorney can confirm who owns the property and get the claim filed correctly.

items.question: The store already mopped up the spill and there were no signs. How can I prove it was there?
items.answer: This is exactly why acting quickly matters. Most retailers along corridors like El Camino Real and Woodside Road run surveillance cameras, and footage is often overwritten within days or weeks unless someone sends a written preservation request. Your own photos, the incident report, receipts showing the time you were there, and any witness contact information all help fill in the picture.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything to find an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service and not a law firm. We connect you with an independent personal injury attorney in our network who handles premises liability cases on contingency, meaning attorney fees are paid only if there is a recovery. Whether you move forward is entirely your decision after speaking with them.
